value.core_idea: Reduce the retained KV cache by discarding tokens deemed unimportant, either via heuristic importance scores computed from attention (SnapKV/H2O/PyramidKV/CAKE) or via learned, task-optimized policies (LKV). The central design axes are (a) the per-token importance indicator (cumulative/mean attention, attention variance, learned utility) and (b) the budget allocation across layers/heads (uniform, fixed pyramid, data-driven preference, or globally learned). Eviction is training-free in the heuristic line and training-aware in the learned line; both preserve the standard attention computation over the retained subset.
value.name: KV Cache Eviction & Token Selection

value.core_idea: Treat the KV cache as a managed, movable resource across the memory hierarchy (GPU HBM, CPU DRAM, remote/disk) and across prefill/decode instances. LMCache provides a standardized caching layer with chunk-level (vs page-level) transfers, asynchronous layer-wise loading overlapped with compute, a shared token pool for cross-instance awareness, and adaptive decisions between KV loading and recomputation depending on bandwidth and context length. The route targets deployment-level metrics (TTFT, ITL, throughput, peak memory) and is orthogonal to accuracy-affecting compression; its gains depend on workload prefix overlap and network bandwidth, with a crossover point below which loading is slower than prefilling.
value.name: System Scheduling & KV Cache Offloading/Disaggregation

value.core_idea: Accelerate decoding by composing speculative/parallel decoding with KV-cache management. QuantSpec uses self-speculative decoding where the draft model loads only an INT4 (upper 4-bit) KV cache and the target model reconstructs INT8 from both halves via a hierarchical INT4 design, eliminating the redundant draft KV copy; a double full-precision buffer (2G) keeps recent tokens in FP16 for high acceptance and clean rollback. The route is grounded in an arithmetic-intensity/roofline analysis that determines when weight quantization vs. KV-cache quantization dominates, and it is most beneficial in long-context memory-bound regimes. It is a cross-route composition (quantization + speculative) distinct from pure eviction or compression.
value.name: Speculative Decoding × KV Cache

value.core_idea: Compress the KV cache by projecting K/V (or their query-aware interactions) into a low-rank subspace, storing only the low-rank factors. KQ-SVD decomposes the query-key interaction KQ^T (not K alone) via truncated SVD, giving a provably optimal closed-form factorization that is robust to K/Q scaling imbalance; it contrasts with K-SVD (compress K alone, ignores Q) and Eigen (joint Q/K/V embedding). The line is training-free but calibration-based (projections learned from a small query set), and trades rank against approximation error of the attention output.
value.name: KV Cache Low-Rank Compression

value.core_idea: Replace or hybridize full softmax attention with fixed-size recurrent/linear-attention memory so the KV cache grows sublinearly (or is constant) with sequence length. NHA unifies, within one layer, a gated linear-RNN long-term memory (m slots) with a sliding-window short-term memory (w tokens) under a unified softmax, and varies w per layer to span pure-linear (w=0), hybrid, or full-attention (w=N) without structural changes; it supports chunkwise parallel training and retrofitting pretrained Transformers. This route trades exact long-range retrieval (bounded by m slots) for sublinear memory and near-linear compute, contrasting with eviction/quantization which keep the Transformer but shrink its cache.
value.name: Architectural Alternatives: Linear/SSM-Attention Hybrids

value.core_idea: Reduce KV cache memory by lowering the numerical precision of stored K/V vectors: scalar quantization (KIVI: per-channel/per-token INT2/INT4) or vector quantization (VQKV: Residual Simple VQ mapping each vector to codebook indices with on-demand reconstruction). QuantSpec extends this to speculative decoding with a hierarchical INT4 cache (upper/lower 4-bit halves) so the draft model uses INT4 and the target reconstructs INT8. The trade-off is compression ratio vs. reconstruction error and the overhead of codebooks/dequantization; scalar methods are training-free, while VQ requires lightweight codebook training.
value.name: KV Cache Quantization & Vector Quantization

value.core_idea: Reduce decoding cost by attending to only a subset of KV tokens selected per query, rather than evicting permanently. NSA is natively trainable hierarchical sparse attention (compressed block + fine-grained selected block + sliding window) co-designed with hardware-aligned kernels so sparsity yields real wall-clock speedup. RocketKV's second stage (HSA) does dynamic two-dimensional top-k selection (sequence + head) using page-wise K_max/K_min statistics, and Quest/SparQ are single-dimension precursors. The route is distinct from eviction because selection is per-query and dynamic, and from architecture because it keeps standard attention over a filtered set.
value.name: Sparse & Dynamic Top-k Attention

value.core_idea: Avoid recomputing KV caches for shared or recurring context (system prompts, retrieved documents, in-context examples) by precomputing, storing, and reusing per-segment KV caches across queries. KVLink enables reuse of independently encoded per-document caches via positional re-encoding (store without RoPE, re-apply global rotations at concat) and trainable link tokens that restore cross-document attention, combined with chunked anchor-token compression. LMCache is the systems substrate: a unified KV caching layer between inference engines (vLLM/SGLang) and heterogeneous storage (GPU/CPU/remote) with chunk-level transfer, async layer-wise loading, and adaptive load-vs-prefill decisions. The route targets the RAG/multi-query and disaggregated-serving settings and is orthogonal to (composable with) compression/eviction.
value.name: Prefix Sharing & KV Cache Reuse Systems
